Chapter Four: Repentance (Part Two). Chapter Four: Repentance. At that time, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa saw in a dream that very night a golden drum; it was magnificent and vast in form, its radiance shining everywhere like the light of the sun.

Furthermore, within the light, they beheld the immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, seated upon lapis lazuli thrones beneath trees made of various jewels, surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands of retinues as they preached the Dharma for them.
He saw a man resembling a Brahmin who struck a drum with a mallet, producing a great sound; that sound proclaimed verses of repentance.

Then, having awakened from his dream, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa mindfully recalled the verses of repentance he had heard within the dream. When night had passed and dawn arrived, he departed from the city of Rājagṛha.
At that time, there were also immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings who, together with the Bodhisattva, went to Vulture Peak Mountain to the place where the Buddha was.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s presence, they prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side. With reverent palms joined and gazing up at the Honored One’s countenance, they spoke to the Tathāgata about the golden drum and the verses of repentance seen in their dreams:
“Last night, in a dream, I held it in my heart with utmost sincerity; I saw a golden drum.”
His wondrous form blazes forth;
its light is most magnificent, surpassing the sun in brilliance as it shines universally throughout the worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions.
One beholds all the Buddhas beneath trees of various jewels, seated upon lapis lazuli thrones,
surrounded by immeasurable multitudes as they preach the Dharma.
Seeing a brahmin strike this golden drum, from the sound of that drum he spoke these verses:
"This great golden drum emits a wondrous sound that is able to utterly extinguish all sufferings of the three periods of time—
the sufferings of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, and so forth."
For those in poverty and distress, as well as all who suffer,
this subtle and wondrous voice can remove the afflictions that oppress sentient beings;
it cuts off all fears and causes them to attain fearlessness, just like the Buddhas.
Attaining fearlessness,
the meritorious virtues accomplished by the Buddhas and sages transcend birth and death, reaching the shore of great wisdom.
The merit, meditative concentration, and factors of enlightenment attained by such sentient beings are like the great ocean.
Through these wondrous sounds produced by this drum, sentient beings are enabled to attain the profound and far-reaching Brahma-voice.
Realizing the unsurpassed, supreme fruit of Bodhi, he turns the unsurpassed wheel, subtle, wondrous, and pure;
dwelling for immeasurable, inconceivable eons, he expounds the True Dharma to benefit sentient beings;
he is able to destroy the afflictions and eliminate all sufferings—greed, hatred, and delusion.
They cause all to be completely extinguished.
Though their bodies are scorched and roasted by a blazing great fire,
if they hear the subtle and wondrous sound of a golden drum and the teachings it proclaims, they immediately seek out and pay homage to the Buddha.
They also cause sentient beings to know their past lives— hundreds of births, thousands of births,
and hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of births;
they cause their minds to maintain right mindfulness of all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and they also hear the unsurpassed, subtle, and wondrous words.
The sublime sounds they emit further cause sentient beings to encounter all Buddhas,
to remain far removed from all evil karmas and the like, and to skillfully cultivate immeasurable pure deeds.
According to their thoughts and whatever they seek to attain,
the sounds produced by this golden drum shall cause them all to achieve and fulfill [their goals].
If there are sentient beings who have fallen into the great hells,
where fierce flames blaze and incinerate their bodies, and for whom there is no protection as they wander through various calamities—
may all such beings have every suffering extinguished.
The torments of all sufferings, the retributions of the three evil realms, and those within the human world—
all these are utterly extinguished by the sounds emitted from this golden drum.
For all those who suffer, who have no support, no refuge,
and no protector, I shall act as their place of refuge.
May these World-Honored Ones now bear witness: long ago, you have already conceived great compassion for me.

Wherever they may be, throughout the ten directions, all Buddhas—the present Heroes of the World, the Honored Ones among two-legged beings—[know] the evil and unwholesome karma that I have previously committed.
Now I repent.
Regarding the kindness of my parents, I failed to understand the wholesome Dharma;
I committed various evils, relying on my own lineage and various wealth and treasures, and was heedless in the prime of my youth.
Committing various evil deeds, with thoughts of unwholesomeness in the mind and performing evil karma with the mouth, acting in accordance with one's inclinations;
failing to see their own faults, the conduct of a foolish worldling, shrouded in the darkness of ignorance;
associating with evil friends, and having a mind distracted by afflictions.
Due to the conditions of the five desires, the mind gives rise to anger and resentment;
lacking knowledge of contentment, one commits various evils. Associating with those who are not noble, one gives rise to stinginess and jealousy due to the conditions of poverty.
Deceitful and sycophantic, one commits evil deeds and remains bound to others.
Constantly living in fear and lacking self-mastery, they commit various evils;
greed, anger, and delusion agitate their minds. Pressed by craving, they perform manifold misdeeds for the sake of food, clothing, and the pleasures of women.
All fetters, afflictions, and fevers, The various evils committed— The three types of karma accumulated through evil deeds of body,
speech, and mind— All such transgressions, I now repent of them all.
Whether out of disrespect toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Noble Sangha,
I now repent all such transgressions;
or out of disrespect toward the Pratyekabuddhas and Bodhisattvas, I now repent all such transgressions.
I now repent of all such transgressions as slandering the True Dharma, lacking reverence for my parents and elders,
acting with arrogance and negligence, and committing various evils due to greed, hatred, and delusion.
All such transgressions, I now repent in their entirety.
I now make offerings to the Buddhas of the immeasurable and boundless three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-systems.
I shall deliver all sentient beings throughout the ten directions from their immeasurable sufferings;
I shall establish inconceivable, asaṃkhyeya multitudes, causing them to dwell in the ten stages.
Having attained stable abiding and dwelling in the ten stages, they cause all to be fully perfected.
For the sake of a single sentient being, they practice for billions of eons, so as to enable immeasurable multitudes to cross the sea of suffering.
For the sake of these sentient beings, I shall expound the subtle and profound Dharma of repentance—
namely, the Golden Light— which eradicates all evils.
If one can, with a sincere heart, perform a single act of repentance, all such transgressions will be entirely extinguished.
This *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* is pure and sublime; it can swiftly eliminate [all sins].
I shall bring all karmic obstacles to rest and abide in the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*), taking the ten kinds of precious jewels as my feet;
attaining the unsurpassed enlightenment of a Buddha, with the radiance of its merit, I shall cause all sentient beings to cross the ocean of the three realms of existence.
May all the Buddhas’ profound treasury of Dharma, Inconceivable and of immeasurable merit,
And the knowledge of all modes— may I fully possess them all;
The hundreds of thousands of meditative concentrations, The faculties, powers, factors of awakening, and the path— may they be inconceivable.
O World-Honored One of Ten Powers! I shall accomplish all the dhāraṇīs.
May the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who possess great compassion, bear witness to my sincere devotion.
Pitifully accept my repentance.
Because of these causes and conditions, I give rise to great sorrow and suffering, poverty and exhaustion, grief, fear, and alarm;
I dread evil karma, and my mind is constantly timid and weak.
In every place and at every moment, there is not even a brief instance of joy.
Throughout the ten directions, the Great Compassionate World-Honored One of the present is able to remove all fears from sentient beings.
I pray that you will accept my sincere repentance, and cause all my fears to be completely eliminated.
I only beseech the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the present age, to use the water of great compassion—
Wash away and purify all past evils; now repent of them all.
As for the offenses committed in the present, I confess them with a sincere heart.
That which has not yet been committed, I dare not commit further;
as for the karma already committed, I dare not conceal it.
Regarding the three types of bodily action, the four types of verbal action, and the three types of mental action—
Now I repent of all that has been done by body and speech, as well as by the mind; I repent of all ten kinds of evil karma.
Staying far removed from the ten unwholesome actions and practicing the ten wholesome ones, dwelling securely in the ten stages and attaining the state of the Honored One of Ten Powers—
whatever evil karma I have created that ought to bring a retribution of suffering, I now repent with a sincere heart before the Buddha.
All wholesome dharmas, I dedicate them all;
The virtues of body, speech, and mind practiced by me— May I, in future lives, realize the Unsurpassed Way.
If, throughout all states of existence, within the perils and difficulties of the six realms of rebirth, we were ignorant and lacking wisdom,
committing various evils— now, before the Buddha, we repent them all.
All that exists in the world— the perils of birth and death, the various difficulties of lustful desire,
and the hardships of ignorance and affliction— I now repent of all such calamities;
as well as the difficulty of a flighty and restless mind, the difficulty of associating with evil friends, and the perils of the three realms of existence.
The difficulty of the three poisons, the difficulty of encountering no calamities, the difficulty of meeting a favorable time,
the difficulty of cultivating merit, and the difficulty of encountering a Buddha— these various difficulties, I now repent of them all.
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are those upon whom I rely; therefore, I now pay homage to the ocean of Buddhas.
Golden and radiantly brilliant, like Mount Sumeru, I now prostrate to the Most Victorious One.
His complexion is unsurpassed, like pure gold;
his eyes are clear and pure, like deep blue lapis lazuli;
his merit, majestic power, and fame are widely renowned.
The Buddha-sun of great compassion extinguishes all darkness; perfectly pure and stainless, it is free from all dust and obscurations.
This unsurpassed Buddha-sun shines its great light everywhere.
The fire of afflictions blazes, causing the mind to wither and burn; only the Buddha can extinguish it, as cool as the moon.
Adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, his body is so magnificent that one never tires of gazing upon it.
His merit is most sublime, and his luminous net shines brilliantly; dwelling peacefully within the triple world, he is like the sun illuminating the world.
Like lapis lazuli, he is pure and free from blemish; his wondrous form is vast and expansive, with various distinct qualities.
Crystal and white silver, with lattices of light as their adornment—
such various things grace the Buddha-sun.
Within the three realms of existence, amidst the great ocean of birth and death, turbulent waters surge and toss about, distressing my mind.
Its taste is bitter and poisonous, most coarse and astringent; yet the Tathāgata Jālinīprabha can cause it to wither and dry up.
His wondrous body is upright and majestic, his marks and signs are extraordinary, and his golden radiance shines everywhere upon all things.
The great ocean of wisdom fills the three realms; therefore, I now bow my head in reverent salutation.
Just as the volume of the waters of the great ocean is difficult to know, so too the atoms of the great earth are beyond calculation.
All the Sumeru mountains are difficult to measure;
even the limits of space cannot be found.
So too it is with all Buddhas: their merits are immeasurable, and no one possessing a mind can know them.
Even if one were to contemplate with the utmost mental effort for immeasurable eons, one could not know the limit of the Buddha’s merit.
The great earth and its mountains might still be measured;
the drops of seawater from a single hair might also be counted.
The merits of all Buddhas are such that none can fully know them.
Adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, their fame and praise— may all beings attain such merits as these.
By virtue of my wholesome karma and through various causes and conditions, before long in a future life, I shall realize the path of Buddhahood.
I will proclaim the sublime Dharma to benefit sentient beings, delivering all from immeasurable sufferings.
Having subdued all Māras and their retinues, you turn the unsurpassed,
pure wheel of Dharma; abiding for immeasurable, inconceivable kalpas,
you satisfy sentient beings with the nectar-like flavor of the Dharma.
I shall fulfill the six pāramitās, just as the Buddhas of the past have accomplished them;
I shall sever all afflictions, eliminate all suffering, and completely extinguish greed,
hatred, delusion, and the like.
I shall recollect the events of my past lives—hundreds of births, thousands of births, and hundreds of thousands of billions of births.
I shall always maintain a sincere heart and right mindfulness toward all Buddhas, and hear the exposition of the subtle and wondrous, unsurpassed Dharma.
By virtue of my wholesome karma, may I always encounter the Buddhas; may I remain far removed from all evils and cultivate all wholesome deeds.
For all sentient beings throughout every world who suffer immeasurable afflictions, I shall extinguish them all.
If there are sentient beings whose faculties are impaired or incomplete, may they all be made complete;
for all those in the worlds of the ten directions who suffer from illness, who are emaciated and exhausted,
and who have no one to protect them, may they all be set free.
May all such sufferings regain their strength and be restored to their original state;
may those who are about to face execution— and who endure immeasurable fear,
sorrow, and affliction— all be set free.
Bound by shackles and fetters, subjected to various forms of suffering that oppress the body in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of ways; with grief, anxiety, and alarm,
and various terrors that disturb the mind— in such immeasurable ways do these manifold afflictions and sufferings prevail.
May all beings without exception attain complete liberation.
If there are sentient beings afflicted by hunger and thirst, may they obtain various kinds of sweet and delicious food and drink;
may the blind see, the deaf hear, and the mute be able to speak.
The naked obtain clothing;
those who are poor immediately find a treasure trove, their storehouses overflowing until they lack for nothing.
All experience peace and happiness, such that not even a single person suffers.
Beings look upon one another with gentle and joyful countenances; their forms are dignified and handsome, pleasing to all who behold them.
Their minds are constantly mindful of the good deeds of others.
With food and drink fully satiated, their merit is complete.
According to what sentient beings think of and desire, may they all obtain every kind of music and entertainment.
The harp, the zither, the flute, the lute, the *śīrṣaka*, and the drums and pipes—
such various and subtle, wondrous sounds;
the rivers, streams, ponds, flowing springs, and all waters, where golden lotuses are strewn about, as well as blue lotuses (*utpala*).
Whatever they think of, they immediately obtain all manner of things: clothing, food and drink,
money and wealth, rare treasures— gold, silver, lapis lazuli, pearls, jade,
and various mixed necklaces.
May all sentient beings never hear evil sounds, nor even encounter anything loathsome to behold.
May all sentient beings possess exquisite physical forms, and may they each regard one another with mutual love and affection.
May all the necessities of life in this world appear to them according to their every thought.
May all beings be fully endowed with these.
May whatever they seek, according to their needs, be obtained immediately upon thought;
and may, throughout the three periods of the day, fine powdered incense and ointments for the body rain down.
Sentient beings who receive [this] shall experience joy and happiness;
they will constantly obtain inconceivable offerings from the Buddhas of the ten directions,
the unsurpassed and wondrous Dharma, which is pure and stainless, as well as from all the Bodhisattvas.
The great assembly of śrāvakas,
having escaped the three evil realms and the eight difficulties, and having found themselves in a place free from such calamities,
behold the Buddhas, the unsurpassed kings.
Abounding in wealth and treasures, secure, peaceful, and prosperous;
with a body adorned by most exquisite forms and features, they have accomplished meritorious virtues and possess great renown.
May all women become men, Possessing wisdom and practicing with tireless diligence;
May they all practice the path of the Bodhisattvas, Diligently cultivating and accumulating the six pāramitās.
Immeasurable Buddhas sit beneath jeweled trees upon seats of lapis lazuli,
abiding in meditative concentration; they dwell in sovereign bliss and proclaim the True Dharma,
which all delight to hear.
Whatever evil karma has been committed, all perils and difficulties, and whatever undesirable results are to be experienced—
may they all be completely extinguished, leaving nothing remaining.
If there are sentient beings bound within the three realms of existence,
caught in the dense and firm net of birth and death— may I, with the sword of wisdom, cut and tear it asunder,
eliminate all suffering and affliction, and cause them to quickly attain Bodhi.
And all other beings throughout immeasurable worlds in other directions—
whatever various, virtuous, and sublime merits they have performed— I now rejoice in them with a profound heart.
And whatever wholesome deeds have been performed by body, speech, and mind,
may they lead to the attainment of the unsurpassed path in future lives, resulting in the auspicious fruit of purity and stainlessness.
If one pays homage and praises the One of Ten Powers with pure faith and free from the net of doubt, and is able to perform such repentance as has been taught,
they shall immediately transcend the sins of sixty kalpas.
As well as virtuous women, kṣatriya kings, and brahmins—
if any among them show reverence, join their palms toward the Buddha,
extol the Tathāgata, and praise this verse— they shall, in every place where they are born, always remember their past lives.
With all faculties complete, pure and dignified, they have fully accomplished every kind of merit;
wherever they may be, they are always revered by kings, ministers, and high officials.
It is not by planting various merits under one Buddha, five Buddhas, or ten Buddhas that one hears this repentance; rather,

it is only after planting various roots of goodness under immeasurable hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions, and billions of Buddhas and Tathāgatas that one is finally able to hear this repentance.

Chapter Five: The Extinction of Karmic Obstructions (2). *The Golden Light Sūtra*, Chapter Five: The Extinction of Karmic Obstructions, translated by Paramārtha, the Tripiṭaka Master of the Liang Dynasty. At that time, the World-Honored One entered the profound dharma-gate of the wondrously named samādhi called "Skillful and Right Discernment. From his pores he emitted various rays of light; hundreds of thousands of immeasurable colors all issued forth from his body. Within these lights, all the buddha-fields appeared clearly.

In the five turbidities of this evil world throughout the ten directions—places beyond the reach of analogies or calculations even by the sands of the Ganges—the light shines forth. All sentient beings therein who have committed the ten non-virtuous actions, the five crimes of immediate retribution, slandered the Triple Gem, failed to be filial toward their parents, or were disrespectful toward śramaṇas, brahmins, and their elders—all those who ought to fall into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals—each receive the light as it reaches the places where they dwell.
When these sentient beings see this light, they shall immediately attain peace and happiness.

By the power of this light, these sentient beings will become upright and exquisite, endowed with perfect physical marks, adorned with merit, and all shall be able to draw near to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
At that time, the great assembly, along with Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the goddess of the Ganges, all came to the place of the gathering and sat to one side.

Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
How do sons and daughters of good family who aspire to seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, practice the Mahāyāna, and embrace all sentient beings?
"How should one repent of these karmic obstructions so as to attain liberation?
The Buddha said,
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Good son!

You now practice this cultivation because you desire to enable immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless sentient beings to attain pure liberation, and out of compassion for the world to bring them peace and happiness."

"Good son! Because all sentient beings fall into various kinds of offenses due to karmic obstructions, they should, throughout the six periods of day and night, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees upon the ground, join their palms in reverence, and with single-minded concentration, speak these words themselves:

'I take refuge and prostrate to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who currently dwell in the worlds of the ten directions and have already attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; who turn the wheel of Dharma, illuminate the wheel of Dharma, uphold the wheel of Dharma, rain down the great rain of Dharma, beat the great drum of Dharma, blow the great conch of Dharma to produce subtle and wondrous sounds, raise the great banner of Dharma, and hold aloft the great torch of Dharma, for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;'"

Practicing the gift of Dharma to guide, receive, and support all sentient beings, for the sake of causing immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings to attain purity and peace and happiness, desiring to cause the great assembly to obtain the great fruit, and for the sake of enabling devas and humans to attain purity.
Thus, one should pay homage to these World-Honored Ones, prostrating with body, speech, and mind in sincere devotion.
These World-Honored Ones, by means of true wisdom, the true eye, true realization, and true equanimity, fully know and fully see the wholesome and unwholesome karma of all sentient beings.

Since beginningless time, following the stream of birth and death, I have already created karmic obstructions together with all sentient beings; bound by greed, hatred, ignorance, and the like, when I did not yet know the Buddha, did not yet know the Dharma, did not yet know the Sangha, and did not yet distinguish between good and evil, I committed immeasurable offenses through my body, speech, and mind.
Due to an evil mind, one sheds the blood of a Buddha, slanders the True Dharma, causes a schism in the Saṃgha, kills an Arhat,
and kills one’s father or mother; one personally commits or instructs others to commit these ten unwholesome paths of action,
rejoices upon seeing them performed, and engages in the three physical, four verbal, and three mental karmic actions, acting with violence toward all sentient beings.
They give rise to disparagement; they deceive others with false measures and scales, taking the counterfeit for the genuine; they bestow impure food and drink upon sentient beings;
they mutually provoke and afflict their parents throughout the six realms of birth and death;

and regarding the property of stupas, the property of the Sangha, and the property of the Sangha from the four quarters, they conceive thoughts of theft and seizure, using it as they please—just as the Buddha has taught.
They speak of the teachings and the Vinaya with excessive error and misguided study; they do not follow the instructions of their teachers and elders;
those who practice as Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or Mahāyānists take delight in reviling one another, causing practitioners to fall into despondency and resentment;
upon seeing those superior to themselves, they harbor jealousy; [and they fail to provide] the gift of Dharma...
They create obstacles by means of material giving; shrouded by ignorance and driven by wrong views and doubt, they cause evil to increase;
they utter harsh words toward the Buddhas, declaring what is Dharma to be non-Dharma, and what is non-Dharma to be Dharma.

All such transgressions, as fully known and seen by the Buddhas through their true wisdom, true eye, true realization, and true equanimity—I now offer confession and repentance before them, disclosing them all without daring to conceal anything. I do not dare to commit again those sins I have not yet committed; those sins already committed, I now confess in their entirety.

Whatever karmic obstructions I have committed that should cause me to fall into the evil realms—the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, or the asuras—and to be born in the twelve places of difficulty, may all such karmic obstructions in this life be entirely extinguished, so that I shall not undergo them in the future.
Just as all the great Bodhisattvas of the past practiced the path to *sambodhi* and fully repented of all their karmic obstructions, so too do I now repent of my karmic obstructions;
I reveal them all and dare not conceal them. May the sins already committed be extinguished, and may I never again commit evil deeds in the future.
Just as all the great Bodhisattvas of the future who cultivate the practices for perfect enlightenment have already repented of all their karmic obstructions;

so too do I now repent of my karmic obstructions, confessing them all openly and not daring to conceal them. May the sins already committed be extinguished, and may I never again commit evil deeds in the future.

Just as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the worlds of the ten directions throughout the present eon have already repented all their karmic obstructions while practicing the path to *sambodhi*, so too do I now repent my own karmic obstructions.
I disclose them all and dare not conceal them; may the sins already committed be extinguished, and I vow never again to commit evil deeds in the future.
Just as all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past, future, and present three periods have repented of their karmic obstructions in this way, so too do I now repent of all my karmic obstructions;
I reveal them all and dare not conceal them. May the sins already committed be extinguished, and may I never again commit evil deeds in the future.
"Therefore, son of good family!
If there is a transgression, one must not conceal it for even a single kṣaṇa, let alone for a day and a night.
Son of good family!"

If one has committed an offense, wishing to attain purity while feeling shame, and believing that there will certainly be retribution in the future, one gives rise to great dread and practices in this manner.
For example, if a man or woman has fire burning their head or fire burning their clothes, they must strive to extinguish it immediately; if the fire is not extinguished, the mind cannot find peace.
It is the same for this son of good family who has committed an offense: he should immediately repent so as to eliminate it, desiring purity in all dharmas and being free from all obstacles.
Having repented in this manner, one shall not dare to commit such offenses again in the future.

"If you wish to be born into a wealthy and prosperous family, where gold, silver, grain, and rice fill the storehouses, and you wish to set forth in the Mahāyāna practice, you should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions.
If you wish to be born into a noble and eminent Brahmin family, fully endowed with the seven treasures, you should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions."
If one wishes to be born into a great and noble family of the Kṣatriya caste or as a Wheel-Turning Sage King (Cakravartin), one should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions;
if one wishes to be born in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, one should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions;

if one wishes to be born in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, or the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, one should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions.
If you wish to be born among the Brahmā-purohita, Brahma-pārṣadya, or Mahābrahmā devas, you should likewise repent and eliminate karmic obstructions;
if you wish to be born among the Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, or Ābhāsvara devas, you should likewise repent and eliminate karmic obstructions;
if you wish to be born among the Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, or Śubhakṛtsna devas, you should likewise repent and eliminate karmic obstructions.

If one wishes to be born in the Heaven Free from Desire, the Heaven Free from Heat, the Heaven of Excellent Appearance, the Heaven of Excellent Vision, or the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, one should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions.
If one seeks the fruit of a Srotāpanna, a Sakṛdāgāmin, an Anāgāmin, or an Arhat, one should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions.

If one aspires to the three knowledges, the six supernormal powers, mastery over bodhi, the ultimate power of a śrāvaka, the great sovereignty of a śrāvaka, or the stage of self-mastery in the bodhi of a pratyekabuddha, one should likewise repent to eliminate karmic obstructions.

If one desires to seek the wisdom of all-knowledge, pure wisdom, inconceivable wisdom, immovable wisdom, and the perfectly complete wisdom of *samyak-saṃbodhi*, one should likewise repent and eliminate karmic obstructions.
Why is this? Son of good family!
All dharmas arise from causes and conditions.

The Tathāgata has taught that there is arising with distinct characteristics and cessation with distinct characteristics due to distinct causes and conditions. At such a time, all past phenomena have already ceased, already been exhausted, and already transformed; thus, these karmic obstructions leave nothing remaining.
These conditioned phenomena, which had not yet manifested in the present, now arise, and future karmic obstructions will no longer arise.
Why is this? Son of good family!
All dharmas are empty, as taught by the Tathāgata; furthermore, there is no sentient being, no life-span possessor, no self or person, no arising or ceasing, and no conditioned phenomena.
“Good son! All dharmas depend upon the root, yet this root itself cannot be described. Why is this?
Because it transcends all marks (*lakṣaṇa*).

If there are sons or daughters of good family who thus enter into the true principle and give rise to faith and reverence, this is called "the absence of sentient beings while having a fundamental basis."
For this reason, it is said that through repentance, one eliminates and extinguishes karmic obstructions.
"Good son! There are four dharmas, when accomplished, by which good sons and good daughters eliminate and extinguish karmic obstructions, attaining eternal purity."
What are these four?

First, the accomplishment of a correct mind; second, recollecting the meaning of profound sutras without giving rise to slander; third, giving rise to the mind of omniscience toward bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds; and fourth, giving rise to immeasurable loving-kindness toward all sentient beings.
"If one can accomplish these four kinds of dharmas, the karmic obstructions resulting from repentance will be forever eliminated.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Single-mindedly protect the three karmas, And do not slander the profound sutras."
"By generating the mind of omniscience and a mind of loving-kindness, one purifies karmic obstacles. 'Good son!
Furthermore, there are four kinds of greatest karmic obstacles that are difficult to purify.'"
What are these four?

First, committing extremely grave offenses against the bodhisattva vows; second, giving rise to slanderous thoughts toward the twelve divisions of the Mahāyāna sūtras; third, being unable to increase any roots of goodness within one's own person; and fourth, being greedily attached to the existence of a mind.
"Furthermore, there are four kinds of remedial methods for extinguishing karmic obstructions.
What are the four?
First, with a sincere heart, draw near to all Tathāgatas throughout the worlds of the ten directions and repent of all transgressions."
Second, to exhort all Buddhas of the ten directions to preach the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings;
third, to rejoice in all merits and virtues accomplished by all sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
fourth, to dedicate all roots of goodness and merit toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how do sons and daughters of good family practice the Mahāyāna?”
“Among those who practice and those who do not practice, how can one rejoice in the roots of merit and goodness of all sentient beings?
The Buddha said, “Good son!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who, during the six periods of day and night, baring their right shoulders, placing their right knees upon the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, single-mindedly speak these words:

"I now rejoice in all the sentient beings of the worlds of the ten directions as they cultivate generosity, cultivate morality, and cultivate meditative concentration; because of this rejoicing as previously described, may all that is sublime, excellent, lovely, unsurpassed, and peerless likewise be rejoiced in;
likewise, I rejoice in all roots of goodness belonging to the past and the future."

Regarding all the merit of the initial generation of the bodhicitta by bodhisattvas in the present age; the great accumulation of merit from practicing the bodhisattva path for more than a hundred great kalpas; the attainment of the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti); the attainment of the stage of non-retrogression; and the accumulation of merit upon reaching the stage of being born only once more before Buddhahood—all such merits as these are rejoiced in and praised, exactly as described above.
Likewise, one likewise rejoices in and praises all the merits of all bodhisattvas of the past and the future.

Now, all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions have already perfected the path to *sambodhi*. For the sake of liberating all sentient beings, they turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, practice the unimpeded gift of Dharma, kindle the great torch of Dharma, beat the great drum of Dharma, blow the great conch of Dharma to produce subtle and wondrous sounds, and raise the great banner of Dharma. All sentient beings receive this gift of Dharma and are fully satisfied; they exhort and transform all beings, causing them all to believe and accept it.

Out of a desire to bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings and out of compassion for all sentient beings—so that all humans and devas may receive peace and happiness, and so that the roots of merit and virtue of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas may all be cultivated and established—I rejoice in and praise those who possess them; and as for any sentient beings who have not yet perfected such merits, I cause them all to become fully endowed with them.
What I have thus spoken is likewise a rejoicing in and praise for all the merits possessed by the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, and the assembly of śrāvakas of the three periods of time.
"In this way, son of good family, one rejoices in an immeasurable and incalculable mass of merit.

For example, suppose all sentient beings in as many worlds as there are in the three-thousandfold world system and as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges were all to become arhats who have extinguished all outflows (āsravas). If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to provide them with the four requisites—robes, food and drink, bedding, and medicine—for as long as they live, the merit of such an act would not equal that of one who cultivates merit by means of sympathetic joy."
Why is this? Because those former merits are finite and measurable, as they do not encompass all merits;
whereas these merits of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*) are immeasurable and innumerable, for they are able to encompass all merits of the three periods of time.
Therefore, noble son!
If there are good men or good women who wish to increase their own roots of goodness, they should rejoice in those who thus cultivate merit;
if there are women who wish to transform their female bodies into male bodies, they should likewise rejoice in those who thus cultivate merit.
At that time, Śakra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will further explain the merit of making this exhortation, so that future bodhisattvas may attain great illumination and present bodhisattvas may fulfill their vows of practice.”
The Buddha said:
"Good son! If there are good sons or good daughters who aspire to seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they should practice the paths of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Mahāyāna."

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the practice, they should, during the six periods of day and night, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees on the ground, join their palms in reverence, and with single-minded concentration, speak these words themselves:

"I pay homage to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout the ten directions, who have now attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and are able to turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma. To them all I now prostrate, entreating them to turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, to kindle the great lamp of Dharma, to uphold the principles of Dharma, to bestow the unimpeded gift of Dharma, to hold aloft the great torch of Dharma, to rain down the great rain of Dharma, to beat the great drum of Dharma, to blow the great conch of Dharma to produce its subtle and wondrous sound, and to raise the great banner of Dharma. For the sake of delivering and liberating all sentient beings, I entreat them as described above, until all humans and devas may receive peace and happiness."
"Furthermore, good son!
If there are good sons or good daughters who wish to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, they should cultivate the practices of the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and the Mahāyāna."

Those who have not yet practiced should, during the six periods of day and night, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees on the ground, join their palms in reverence, and with single-minded focus, speak these words:

"I prostrate to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout the worlds of the ten directions who wish to relinquish their response-bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*) and enter *nirvāṇa*. I now entreat you not to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, but to remain long in the world to deliver, liberate, and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, as previously described, so that even humans and devas may all receive peace and happiness."

I now dedicate all the roots of goodness and merit from this exhortation toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, just as all the merits of the great bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present are entirely dedicated toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
I likewise dedicate all the merits of my exhortations toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

“Good son! Suppose a good man or a good woman were to offer the seven treasures filling the entire trichiliocosm as an offering to the Tathāgata; yet if another good man or good woman were to exhort the Tathāgata to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma, the merit of that exhortation would surpass the former.”
Why is this? These supreme roots of goodness are the gift of material wealth, while the merit of exhortation is the gift of the Dharma. "Good son!

Setting aside the seven treasures filling a trichiliocosm, suppose there were as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, and a son or daughter of good family were to fill those worlds with the seven treasures and offer them to all the Buddhas; yet the merit of a son or daughter of good family who exhorts and entreats the Tathāgata to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma would surpass that of the former.
Why is this? Because there are five kinds of matters regarding the gift of Dharma. What are these five?
First, the gift of Dharma benefits both oneself and others, whereas the gift of material wealth does not;
second, the gift of Dharma enables sentient beings to transcend the triple world, whereas the gift of material wealth does not lead beyond the realm of desire;
third, the gift of Dharma nourishes the Dharma-body, whereas the giver of material wealth increases only the physical body.
Fourth, the gift of Dharma increases without end, whereas material gifts are inevitably exhausted;
fifth, the gift of Dharma can sever ignorance, while material gifts merely suppress the greedy mind.
Therefore, good son!
The merit of making this request is immeasurable and incalculable, beyond the reach of analogy.
Just as when I was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, I made requests, as previously described, to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, to turn the great wheel of Dharma;
Because of these roots of goodness, all the Śakras and Great Brahmā Kings entreated me to turn the great wheel of Dharma, saying:
"World-Honored One!
We pray that you will turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of liberating and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings, as well as to all humans and devas."

"In the past, while practicing for the sake of Bodhi, I exhorted the Tathāgatas to remain long in the world and not enter parinirvāṇa; by virtue of these merits, I have attained the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness and great compassion, and immeasurable, innumerable unique qualities."
I have already entered into *nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa*, yet my True Dharma shall abide long in the world.

My Dharma-body is incomparable and pure, possessing various marks, immeasurable wisdom, immeasurable sovereignty, and inconceivable, immeasurable merit. All sentient beings receive its profound and compassionate nourishment; even if one were to speak for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *kalpas*, it could never be fully described.
Therefore, the Dharma-body is able to contain and conceal all phenomena, yet all phenomena cannot contain or conceal the Dharma-body. The Dharma-body is eternally abiding;
it does not fall into the view of eternalism, and though it may appear to cease, it does not fall into the view of nihilism.

It shatters the various views of all sentient beings and can give rise to all manner of true insights. It can resolve that the bonds of all sentient beings are not different from liberation itself. It can plant the roots of all kinds of goodness for all sentient beings, bring to maturity the roots of goodness of all sentient beings, and enable those already matured to attain liberation. It is without action, without movement, unconditioned, and tranquil; it is peaceful, sovereign, and far removed from clamor. It transcends the three periods of time yet can perceive the three periods of time; it surpasses the realms of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. It is the practice of the great earth bodhisattvas, and all Tathāgatas are of one and the same essence.
By the power of the roots of goodness from the merit of exhortation, I have now attained such a Dharma-body.
Therefore, son of good family!

If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, for the sake of attaining anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, uphold even a single phrase or a single verse to exhort and transform others, and explain it to them, the roots of goodness of their merit are difficult to measure; how much more so for those who exhort the Tathāgata to turn the great wheel of Dharma and to remain long in the world, not entering parinirvāṇa?
At that time, Śakra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How do good men and good women, for the sake of attaining anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, practice the paths of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Mahāyāna?”
“If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the roots of goodness from practicing merit, how can they all dedicate [their merit] toward the wisdom of omniscience?
The Buddha said, “Good son!
If there are good sons or good daughters who wish to seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and practice the paths of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or the Mahāyāna;
If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the practice, and for one day and one night with single-minded devotion they speak these words themselves:

"All roots of goodness that I have accumulated since beginningless birth and death are already perfected; whether toward the Triple Gem, or toward others—even down to animals, humans, and non-humans—I have offered even a mere handful to all beings, and furthermore, I have used kind words to reconcile quarrels, taken the three refuges, and trained in the precepts. All these merits and roots of goodness are obtained through repentance, obtained through sympathetic joy, and obtained through exhortation."

These roots of goodness are placed together, grasped simultaneously, gathered and weighed; all are dedicated for the benefit of all sentient beings, having been relinquished forever, with no further thought of reclaiming them, liberated and unrestrained.

Just as the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—the knowers and the seers—possess Buddha-wisdom that is inconceivable, unimpeded, and stainless, and thus dedicate all such meritorious roots of virtue to all sentient beings with a mind that neither dwells on signs nor abandons signs;

so too do I dedicate all my merits and roots of virtue to all sentient beings, wishing that all sentient beings may obtain the "Precious Hand," which extracts jewels from emptiness to fulfill the wishes of all beings, such that their wealth and joy are inexhaustible, their merit is inexhaustible, the sublime Dharma is inexhaustible, their sovereignty is inexhaustible, and their four analytical knowledges are inexhaustible.
For the sake of attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and for the sake of attaining the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), I now bestow upon all sentient beings my roots of merit and virtue;

from these roots of virtue, may further immeasurable roots of all goodness be obtained, which I shall gather together, weigh, and dedicate entirely toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. By virtue of these roots of goodness, may I share them with all sentient beings so that we may together reach *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and attain the knowledge of all modes.

Just as in the past, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practiced the path to enlightenment, they dedicated all their merits and roots of goodness toward the attainment of all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*);

so too do I dedicate all my merits and roots of goodness toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. By virtue of these roots of goodness, I shall share them with all sentient beings, so that together we may simultaneously attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the sake of obtaining the wisdom of all-knowledge.
Just as the merits and roots of goodness of future bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should also be dedicated so that they may, together with all sentient beings, attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
so too do I likewise dedicate all my merits and roots of goodness, as extensively explained above.

Just as present bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate their merits and roots of goodness toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, so that they may attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* together with all sentient beings;
I shall likewise share all my merits and roots of goodness with sentient beings, as explained extensively above.

Just as other Buddhas sit at the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree—inconceivable, stainless, and pure—abiding in the *śūraṅgama-samādhi*, the *dhāraṇī* of the inexhaustible treasury of Dharma, they shatter the immeasurable hosts of the Māra Pāpīyān; and that which should be seen, known, awakened to, and thoroughly realized—all such things they fully illuminate and comprehend in a single kṣaṇa, attaining the path of ambrosia and obtaining the Dharma of ambrosia during the final watch of the night.

I, too, am likewise: sharing the same roots of goodness with all sentient beings, by virtue of these roots of goodness, we shall together attain the path of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and equally obtain the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).
"Just as [it was with] Amitāyus Buddha,
Suprabha Buddha,
and Arciṣmanta Buddha..."
Akṣobhya Buddha,
Guṇasūryaprabha Buddha,
and Siṃhaprabha Buddha.
Buddha Hundred Radiance,
Buddha Net Radiance,
and Buddha Jewel Mark.
Ratnārci Buddha,
Arci-prabhāsa Buddha,
and Arci-samṛddha-prabhāsa Buddha.
Buddha Anjishangwang,
Buddha Wēimiàoshēng,
Buddha Miàozhuāngyán.
Dharmadhvaja Buddha,
Uttamakāya Buddha,
and Samantapriyadarśana Buddha.
The Tathāgatas Prabhāsa-vyūha,
Brahma-viśuddha-rāja,
and Uttama-gotra, and all such Tathāgatas as these.
The Arhat,
the Samyaksaṃbuddha, of the past and the future.
Now they all manifest through transformation and response,
attaining unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment and turning the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma.
Desiring to deliver and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, he has extensively taught as above;
I, too, am likewise, and together with all sentient beings, shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and turn the Great Wheel of Dharma, as extensively taught above.

“If any good man or good woman takes up, maintains, recites, and memorizes without forgetting this ‘Chapter on the Destruction of Karmic Obstructions’ from the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the king of all sutras, and explains it extensively for others, they will possess an immeasurable, innumerable, and vast accumulation of merit.”

Suppose that every single sentient being throughout the trichiliocosm, without any distinction of before or after, were to achieve a human body, and having attained a human body, were to realize the path of a pratyekabuddha.

If there are good sons or good daughters who, for as long as they live, respectfully prostrate to and provide the four types of offerings to each and every pratyekabuddha—supplying each one with the seven treasures in quantities like Mount Sumeru—and if, once each of these pratyekabuddhas has entered nirvana, they erect stupas made of the seven treasures for them;
[the merit of this would not equal that of hearing this sutra].
Each of these stupas is made entirely of the seven treasures. What are the seven?
They are gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, agate, musaragalva, and blue and yellow jewels.

That stupa was twelve yojanas in height and breadth; at that site of the stupa, they made offerings with various flowers, incense, precious banners, flags, and canopies—each and every article of offering.
"Good son, what do you think?
Would these good sons and good daughters acquire much merit?"
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Good son! This *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*—this subtle and wondrous scripture, the king of all sūtras—the ‘Chapter on the Extinction of Karmic Obstructions,’ you should receive, uphold, read, recite, and remember it without forgetting, and explain it extensively for others. Compared to the mass of merit obtained later from the roots of goodness of the aforementioned virtues, [the latter] does not equal even one hundredth part, nor one hundred-thousand-myriad-billionth part; it cannot be reached by calculation or analogy.”

Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family abide in right practice, entreating the World-Honored Ones, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, in the Buddha-fields of the ten directions to turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, thereby causing all Tathāgatas to rejoice and offer their praise.
“Good son! As I have taught, among all forms of giving, the gift of Dharma is supreme.
Therefore, good son, the offerings made to the Triple Gem cannot be compared [to it].”
The observance of the three refuges and all the precepts cannot be compared [to this];
the non-emptiness of the Three Jewels cannot be compared [to this];
and the exhortation for the Three Jewels of all worlds throughout the three periods of time to abide long cannot be compared [to this].
The exhortation for the Tathāgata to preach the profound and correct Dharma throughout all worlds of the three periods of time for immeasurable eons cannot be compared [to this];
the exhortation for all sentient beings in all worlds, according to their strength, capacity, and inclination, to resolve upon bodhicitta within the three vehicles cannot be compared [to this];
causing all sentient beings in all worlds of the three periods of time to become unimpeded and swiftly achieve the fulfillment of merit cannot be compared [to this].
Exhorting all sentient beings in all worlds throughout the three periods of time to attain unimpeded, perfect enlightenment (samyak-saṃbodhi) cannot be compared [to this];
exhorting all sentient beings in all worlds throughout the three periods of time to emerge from the four evil realms cannot be compared [to this];
exhorting all sentient beings in all worlds throughout the three periods of time to extinguish deep and grave karmic obstacles cannot be compared [to this].
It cannot be compared to exhorting all beings to attain liberation from every form of suffering and affliction;
it cannot be compared to exhorting them to attain liberation from every fear, hardship, and urgent distress;

nor can it be compared to rejoicing in all the merits and roots of goodness possessed by all sentient beings before the Buddhas of the three periods of time, or to personally generating the vow for bodhicitta throughout the three periods of time.

Excluding misconduct, verbal abuse, and the paths of unwholesome karma, may all roots of merit and virtue be gathered and sustained. In birth after birth, may I exhort and reverently make offerings to the Triple Gem; exhort and pray that all pure meritorious deeds may lead to the fulfillment of the path to *samyak-saṃbodhi*; exhort and pray for the perfection of the six *pāramitās*; exhort and pray for the turning of the unsurpassed Wheel of Dharma; and exhort and pray that [the Buddhas] remain for immeasurable eons to preach immeasurable, profound, and wondrous teachings—none of which can be compared [to this].

At that time, Śakra, the goddess of the Ganges, immeasurable Brahmā kings, and the four heavenly kings rose from their seats; each baring his right shoulder, placing his right knee upon the ground, and joining his palms in prostration at the Buddha’s feet, addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We have all now heard this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of all sutras; we shall now receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain it for others, and we should abide in accordance with this Dharma.
Why is this? World-Honored One!
It is because we seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; it is for the sake of following this principle and practicing the various marks of the True Dharma.
At that time, the Brahma King, Śakra the Lord of Devas, and all others gathered like clouds at the place where the Dharma was being taught, scattering various *mandārava* flowers over the Buddha.

The earth of the trichiliocosm shook violently; all celestial drums and various musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck; and golden light was emitted, pervading the entire world, with these words issuing forth:

"This subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra extends its compassionate grace universally, providing manifold benefits, manifold increases to the roots of goodness of Bodhisattvas, and extinguishing all karmic obstructions."
The Buddha said:
"So it is, so it is; it is just as you have said. Why is this?"
"Good son!

I recall that in the past, extending back through hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kalpas until this present life, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnarāja-mahādīptaprabhā appeared in the world and remained in that world for six hundred and eighty billion kalpas."

In the first assembly, hundreds of thousands of billions of trillions of beings all attained arhatship; their outflows were exhausted, they possessed the six supernormal powers, and they were sovereign and unimpeded.

In the second assembly, ninety thousand billions of trillions of beings attained arhatship; all had their outflows exhausted, and they attained mastery in the three knowledges and the six supernormal powers.

In the third great assembly, ninety-eight thousand billions of trillions of beings all attained arhatship, possessing the three knowledges and the six supernormal powers with sovereign non-obstruction.

At that time, the Tathāgata Jewel King Great Blazing Radiance appeared in the world for the sake of delivering, liberating, and bringing peace and happiness to all devas, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and the common people.

“Good son! At that time, I was in the body of a woman named Puṇyaratnaprabhā. During the third assembly, I approached the World-Honored One at the place of the gathering, received, upheld, read, and recited this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra*, and expounded it extensively for others, in order to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Therefore, the World-Honored One bestowed upon me this prediction:

"This woman, Puṇyaratnaprabhā, shall in a future age attain Buddhahood, and her name shall be Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."

"After casting off that female body, from that time forward I have transcended the four evil realms and been born among gods and humans to experience supreme and wondrous bliss. Eighty-four hundred thousand times I became a wheel-turning monarch, and reaching until this day, I have attained Buddhahood, my fame being universally heard and filling the entire world."

At that time, the assembly beheld the Tathāgata Jewel King Great Blazing Radiance turning the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma and preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma. From this Sahā world, proceeding eastward past as many Buddha-fields as there are sands in hundreds of thousands of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Jewel Adornment; he remains there even now, has not yet entered parinirvāṇa, and is preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma to extensively transform sentient beings.

"Furthermore, if any son or daughter of good family hears the name of this Tathāgata Ratnarāja Mahādīptaprabha, they shall attain non-retrogression on the bodhisattva stages until their final parinirvāṇa."

If there is a woman who hears the name of this Tathāgata, King of Jewels Great Blazing Radiance, at the time of her death she shall behold the World-Honored One coming to her side; having beheld the Buddha, she will ultimately never again receive a female body.
“Good son! This subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* brings about manifold benefits and manifold increases in the roots of goodness of bodhisattvas, and extinguishes all karmic obstructions.”

“Good son! If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who, wherever they may be, preach and expound this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra for others, that land shall all obtain four kinds of roots of merit and goodness.”
What are the four?
First, the king shall be free from all illnesses and afflictions, as well as all calamities and misfortunes;
second, his lifespan shall be long and far-reaching, without any obstacles.
Third, there shall be no enemies or adversaries; the military forces will be brave and strong, such that none can defeat them.
Fourth, there will be peace, security, and happiness, and the sublime Dharma will constantly flourish.
Why is this? Because such a king of men is constantly protected by Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the hosts of yakṣas.
O noble son!
“Is this so? These immeasurable Śakras, Brahmās, Four Great Kings, and hosts of yakṣas all answered the World-Honored One with one voice: “It is so, it is so.”
If this sutra is expounded in any kingdom or territory, we—the Four Great Kings—and all the kings of those lands shall constantly come to protect them, accompanying them in their walking and staying.
Should those kings encounter any calamities, obstacles, or enemies, we, the Four Great Kings, shall be able to ward them off;
should they suffer from illness, affliction, or any unpleasant conditions, we shall cause them all to be healed and their lifespans increased.
Regarding the Dharma of auspiciousness and the Dharma of endearment, we have the power to inspire hearts of joy;
we can also ensure that all of your troops become valiant and robust.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"
As you have said, you should practice accordingly. Why is this?
When these kings practice in accordance with the Dharma, all the people follow the king in their cultivation.

"If there are people who are able to practice in accordance with the Dharma, you all shall receive the benefits of physical strength and beauty, your palaces shall be radiant, and your retinues shall be powerful.
The Śakras, Brahmās, and others replied to the Buddha, "So it is."
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:
“In this land, wherever this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* is expounded, the various kingdoms, great ministers, and prime ministers shall receive four kinds of grace.”
First, they treat one another with mutual intimacy, respect, affection, and patience;
second, they are always revered by human kings and protected by śramaṇas, brahmins, great kingdoms, and small kingdoms;
third, they value the Dharma over wealth, do not seek personal gain or fame, and their reputation spreads far and wide, such that all people praise and look up to them.
Fourth, their lifespan will be long, and they will dwell in peace and happiness—these are the four kinds of meritorious benefits.
If there is a land where this sutra is proclaimed, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and others shall obtain these four kinds of merit.
What are the four?
First, clothing, food and drink, bedding, and medicine;
second, that all may find peace of mind for sitting in meditation and reciting the scriptures.
Third, dwelling in peace and happiness by relying on mountain forests;
fourth, attaining fulfillment according to one's wishes by relying on the mind.
These are called the four kinds of merit.

If there is a land where this sutra is preached and proclaimed, all its people shall attain abundance and joy, be free from all epidemics, and merchants and travelers shall obtain much precious wealth; being endowed with these four blessings, this is called the manifold merit and benefit.
At that time, Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Great Kings, and the great assembly in this gathering addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

As for the profound meaning of such a sūtra as this, if it were in the present age, the Tathāgata’s thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and other teachings would still abide in the world and not yet have perished.”
"If this sutra should perish, the True Dharma will also perish.
The Buddha said:
"Therefore, son of good family!"

With such characteristics, if one single-mindedly and correctly hears, single-mindedly and correctly upholds, single-mindedly and correctly contemplates, single-mindedly and correctly recites, or single-mindedly and extensively explains to others even a single phrase, a single verse, a single chapter, or a single section of this *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra*, they will enjoy peace and happiness throughout the long night.

The Combined Edition of the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra, Volume III.
